decks.name: LeetCode #56 - Merge Intervals
decks.description: Merge all overlapping intervals in a collection

cards.question: Merge Intervals: Given an array of intervals where intervals[i] = [starti, endi], merge all overlapping intervals, and return an array of the non-overlapping intervals that cover all the intervals in the input.

solutions.name: Sorting
solutions.explanation: Sort intervals by start time first. Initialize result with first interval. For each subsequent interval, check if it overlaps with last interval in result (start <= last end). If overlaps, merge by extending last interval's end to maximum of both ends. If no overlap, add as new interval to result. Sorting ensures we process intervals in order, making single pass sufficient. Most intuitive and commonly used approach. O(n log n) time due to sorting.

solutions.name: Sweep Line Algorithm
solutions.explanation: Treat interval boundaries as events on timeline. For each interval, mark start as +1 event (interval begins) and end as -1 event (interval ends). Sort all events by position. Sweep through timeline: when counter becomes non-zero, interval starts; when counter returns to zero, interval ends. Track active interval count to determine when intervals merge or separate. Classic computational geometry technique. O(n log n) time due to sorting events.

solutions.name: Greedy
solutions.explanation: Use array indexed by coordinate values for O(1) access. Find max start value to size array. For each interval, store its end+1 at start position (marks furthest reach). Sweep through array: when non-zero value found, start new interval and track furthest endpoint seen. When current position equals tracked endpoint, close interval. Works well when coordinate range is small. O(n+m) time where m is max coordinate value. Trade-off: faster than sorting when m < n log n, but uses more space.
